title: Ready for a public repository
description: Can a file be published in a public GitHub repository as it is? One question per risk: personal data, outside paths, private links, language, third-party content, leftovers. The gate sends one patch per staged file. Every answer is the probability that the file is fine on that axis. .jev-check-example/fixtures/public-release/ holds the cases that set its threshold.

no_personal_info.instructions: Is the patch in `files` free of personal information about the author or their machine?

criteria.true: No added line holds a personal home path such as /home/<user> or /Users/<user>, a personal or work email address, a username, a machine or sandbox name, or a real person's name. Placeholders such as <user>, you@example.com, and $HOME are fine.
criteria.false: An added line holds a personal home path, an email address, a username, a machine or sandbox name, or a real person's name.

no_outside_paths.instructions: Does the patch in `files` avoid naming folders or projects that live outside this repository on the author's machine?

criteria.true: Every local path in the patch is inside this repository or is a standard system path.
criteria.false: A path names a sibling project, a parent folder, or a home folder that is not part of this repository.

no_private_links.instructions: Is the patch in `files` free of links and host names that a stranger cannot reach, such as internal company hosts, private repositories, or ticket and chat links?

criteria.true: Every link and host is public, including public APIs and docs the project uses, or there are none.
criteria.false: A link or host is internal, private, or only reachable from the author's network.

english_only.instructions: Could an English-only reader read every comment, message, and doc line added in the patch in `files`?

criteria.true: Yes. There are no sentences in another language.
criteria.false: No. At least one sentence is written in another language, such as Portuguese or Spanish.

no_third_party_content.instructions: Is the patch in `files` free of copied third-party content that the project has no clear right to publish?

criteria.true: The content is the project's own, or short quotes, or material with a license that allows it and credits the source.
criteria.false: An added line holds a copied article, blog post, book text, another project's files, or a scraped web page, without a license that allows publishing it.

belongs_in_project.instructions: Does the file in `files` serve the purpose in `project`, rather than being a leftover from an experiment or another project?

criteria.true: The file is code, docs, config, a test, or an example that this project uses or documents.
criteria.false: The file is a scratch note, an experiment, a stray output, or sample data or config for a different project.
